what_happened.line: Commissioners said informally they are open to extending the sewer service area to a Chestnut Street horse-rescue parcel, but want formal plans first.
The applicant would seek a citizen petition for town meeting; the commission took no vote on the extension.
Staff will keep ARPA funds on the agenda and seek clarification, since Treasury guidance suggests sewer money may be limited to revolving-fund-eligible projects.
The engineering contract for the Upland, Eastern Ave and White Street extension is back from counsel with redlines, and soil borings are planned.
The assistant business manager job was re-advertised as a benefited role, and a first draft of the FY23 sewer budget is due on the January 25 agenda.

why_it_matters: Extending the sewer district to a new parcel needs town meeting action by citizen petition, so residents may be asked to vote on it.
Whether ARPA money can pay for the pump station plan is unresolved, and the answer could affect what sewer ratepayers cover through rates.
watch_next: January 25 meeting: first draft of the FY23 sewer budget, Q3 billing, and a possible Fitchburg sewer use ordinance item.
Any citizen petition for town meeting on the Chestnut Street sewer service area, and the ARPA eligibility clarification.
